title: Flared Inlet Apron and Pierced Culvert Headwall
description: One original static village drainage-interface visual module: a complete grounded rectangular apron receives two whole outward-flared side wings that rise toward a thick end headwall. The end wall has a genuine low full-depth rectangular culvert opening, while the widening inlet remains open above and at the front. Each wing meets the apron along its whole bottom and the headwall along a finite rear face; four separately editable closed meshes form one asset. The 0.34 by0.24m rear aperture is illustrative; no old road, culvert, drain, fence or receiver mesh is imported or modified, and no installation with old joined assets is claimed. This is a wide-open-mouth to covered-mouth transition, not the existing right-angle drop drain, a whole covered road culvert or an extracted terminal post. No water, road, grate, moving gate or hidden host. No hydraulic, retention, erosion, structural load, vehicle, engineering, construction, safety or module-fit performance is represented.
